capex.item: EV/clean mobility capex of close to INR300 crores is planned for next financial year across all four businesses.

capex.quote: we got the environment clearance for the commercial facility. As far as the semi-commercial plant is concerned, at this juncture, are doing validation batches for the first DMF, which is likely to come up the next two quarters.

capex.delivered: Plant operational and ramping, but 100% utilisation now guided to end-FY27 or middle of FY28
capex.item: The new CRSS facility at Nasik will complete customer approvals in three to four months and be fully operational by Q3 of FY26, with full utilisation expected in Q3-Q4.

capex.quote: the third part of course is battery, where as we start packing our batteries here, which will happen towards the end of this year, then that will also bring down prices more.

capex.item: The new CRS plant at Nasik and tube plant at Phaltan are ramping utilisation and are expected to be fully booked by the first quarter of next year.

business.body: Engineering: Rev Rs.1,495cr (+21.6% YoY), PBIT Rs.176cr; Metal Formed: Rev Rs.421cr (+4.5% YoY), PBIT Rs.35cr (-10% YoY) impacted by Hyundai muted growth/railway tender margins; Mobility (EV): Rev Rs.208cr (+14.9% YoY), PBIT Rs.4cr (flat); Volumes: 87 Big Trucks, 241 SCV, 1,176 Three-wheelers; Medical: Rev Rs.246cr (+0.8% YoY), PBIT Rs.16cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain bottleneck resolved by in-house takeover | Tube Investments of India Ltd | beneficiary | High | BIW facility acquisition removes structural cap on 3W volumes; immediate ramp expected in Q1 FY27. |
| Commodity inflation lag and railway tender margin pressure | Shanthi Gears Ltd | loser | Med | Revenue declined 11.8% YoY; margin compression in gear segment due to product mix and slower industrial demand. |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: Tube Investments of India Limited manufactures a broad range of engineered products organised into segments including precision steel tubes and strips (Engineering), metal-formed products such as automotive chains and railway wagon sections, mobility products including standard and specialty bicycles, and gears, motors and drives. The Company has expanded into Power Systems (transformers, switchgears, automation and turnkey projects), semiconductors (OSAT and fabless design), and new-venture electric vehicles.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Engineering:** Cold Drawn Welded (CDW) Tubes, Electric Resistance Welded (ERW) Tubes, Tubular Components, Cold Rolled Steel Strips (CRSS)
- **Metal Formed Products:** Automotive Chains, Fine Blanked Products, Roll-Formed Car Doorframes, Cold rolled formed sections for Railway Wagons & Passenger Coaches, Industrial Chains
- **Mobility:** Standard Bicycles, Special Bicycles including Alloy Bikes, Speciality Performance Bikes, Fitness Equipment, E-Bicycles
- **Gears:** Gears, Gear Boxes, Gear Motors, Gear & Gear Products, Electric Motors, Alternators, Drives, Traction, Electronic & SCADA, Industrial Systems
- **Power Systems:** Transformers, Switchgears, Automation & Turnkey Projects
- **Semiconductor:** Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT), Fabless Semiconductor Design Business, TMT, TI Optoelectronic Solutions
- **New Ventures (Electric Vehicles):** E-Three Wheeler, E-Tractor, E-M&HCV, E-SCV
business.title: Products & brands

business.body: - Diversified multi-segment engineering portfolio spanning tubes, metal-formed products, mobility, gears/motors, power systems and semiconductors, reducing dependence on any single end market
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: TII delivered robust consolidated growth (Revenue +21% YoY) driven by CG Power and core Engineering, while standalone EV mobility faced temporary supply constraints now resolved via in-house capacity capture. The strategic pivot to internalize body-in-white production and pending railway certifications positions FY27 for accelerated volume recovery despite near-term commodity cost headwinds.

open.item: In-house battery packing (Manesar plant) is to be operational towards the end of FY26, which will bring EV component prices down further.
TI Clean Mobility EV volumes for FY26 will definitely be higher than the previous year.
Small commercial vehicle network to go from 2 fully operational dealers to 25 across the country, and e-tractor from 4 to about 25 fully operational dealerships before the end of FY26.
open.promised: 25 dealers each for SCV and e-tractor dealers

open.item: The new Nasik plant adds about 7-8% incremental capacity to the engineering division, roughly 4,000 tonnes per month.
open.promised: 4000 tonnes per month; 7-8% incremental engineering capacity tonnes per month

open.item: EV/clean mobility capex of close to INR300 crores is planned for next financial year across all four businesses.

Having taken over the body-in-white supplier's facility, management is confident of resolving the body-in-white bottleneck by and large by the end of Q1FY27, with April and May ramp-up already at targeted levels.
open.promised: issue resolved by end of quarter text

open.item: After a body-in-white supplier issue cut Q4 three-wheeler output to 50% of potential, management is confident of returning to normal production capacity by the end of Q1FY27.
open.promised: back to normal production capacity text

CG Power is recruiting one or two key people to drive growth of the services business, with the team expected to be on board in Q1 FY2027 before growth starts.

open.promised: commercial production starting next quarter date

open.promised: commercial production start after Q1-Q2 approvals date

open.item: TI Clean Mobility has a good order book for heavy electric trucks and expects to deploy these trucks in Q1 and Q2 of FY27 once financing and charging infrastructure bottlenecks are untangled.
open.promised: deployment in Q1 and Q2 text

open.item: The new engineering plant in the West is deferred and expected to be delayed by six to nine months due to machine supplier challenges.
The CRSS plant at Nasik is ramping up and is expected to reach 100% utilisation by end of FY27 or the middle of FY28.
A rough-cut estimate of around Rs.300 Crores is planned to be invested into subsidiaries (TICMPL EV business and TI Medical) in FY27.
FY27 capex in the standalone core business is guided at around Rs.300 Crores to Rs.350 Crores.
Management reiterated confidence in growing the wound care / suture business at 15% to 20%.

open.horizon: two to three quarters from Q1FY27
open.item: Railway product development is complete but customer approvals with Government of India for Vande Bharat coaches are pending; management expects some visible progress two to three quarters from now.
European demand is weak and MFPD exports to Europe are a drag; any EU FTA benefit will come with a lag of around 12 to 15 months and non-tariff barriers such as CBAM remain a challenge.
Tube facilities in the Western region have reached about 30% capacity utilisation and management is hopeful of 100% utilisation by the middle of the next financial year.

revisions.item: Management reiterated confidence in double-digit growth (including on EBITDA) for the standalone business, subject to export headwinds.
Management is hopeful of delivering 20% year-on-year growth in TI Medical going forward, aided by the newly acquired IV cannula business.

wtt.tone_latest: Confident and bullish on demand and new-vertical growth, with management explicitly owning misses — the Q4 three-wheeler volume hit from the body-in-white supplier (only 50% of potential output), the repeatedly delayed railway scale-up, sluggish MFPD, and the muted medical devices exports.
